findings.finding: Insights: From sum equality after giving 5 sweets, get B+b=10 and A+a=20. Substitute a=20‑A, b=10‑B. Solve integer equations A(20‑A)=4B(10‑B) and A(15‑A)=B(15‑B) with 1≤A≤15,1≤B≤10, a≥5. Unique solution A=10,B=5 → product = 50. Pitfall: ensure sweets non‑negative and a≥5.

Insights: From sum equations get b+B=10, a+A=20. Set A=20‑a, B=10‑b. Use product equations: a(20‑a)=4b(10‑b) and a(15‑a)=b(15‑b). Search integer ages 1‑15,1‑10 → only (a,b)=(10,5). Product=50. Pitfall: ensure sweets non‑negative, A≥5.

Insights: Let a,b ages; x,y sweets. From “sum double” and “after giving 5 sweets sums equal”: a+x=2(b+y) and a+x-5=b+y+5 ⇒ a+x=20, b+y=10. Use product equations: a·x=4b·y and a·(x‑5)=b·(y+5). Substitute a=20‑x, y=10‑b. Solve integer x∈[5,19], b∈[1,10] → only (a,b,x,y)=(10,5,10,5). Age product =10·5=50. Pitfall: assume sweets non‑negative; ages positive.
